calories-burned-calculator.assumptionNote: MET values are population averages. Fitness level, terrain, speed and effort shift your real burn, so treat the result as a solid estimate, not a measurement.
benefits: Instantly compares which activities give you the most burn per minute.
Weight-adjusted results are fairer than generic per-hour tables.
Helps you budget exercise into a weekly calorie plan.

faqs.a: A MET is a metabolic equivalent: 1 MET is your resting burn, about 1 kcal per kg per hour. An 8-MET activity burns roughly eight times your resting rate.
A 70 kg person burns about 343 kcal in 30 minutes running at 10 km/h, 105 kcal walking slowly, or 280 kcal swimming moderately. Heavier people burn proportionally more.
faqs.q: How many calories do common activities burn?

faqs.a: Fitness watches estimate from heart rate and movement, which adds personal data but also sensor error. MET tables use averages and are surprisingly close for steady activities.
faqs.q: Are fitness watch calories more accurate?

faqs.a: No. Spot reduction is a myth. Exercise burns calories across the whole body; where you lose fat first is genetic.
faqs.q: Can I target belly fat with exercise?

faqs.a: About 60-70% of your daily burn is BMR and digestion, not exercise. That is why diet matters more for weight loss, while exercise matters more for health and keeping weight off.
faqs.q: Why does exercise matter if it burns so few calories?

faqs.a: You cannot out-train a bad diet: a 500 kcal dessert takes over an hour of running to offset. Use exercise for fitness and food for weight control.
faqs.q: Can I out-train a bad diet?

calories-burned-calculator.formula:
Calories = MET x weight (kg) x hours.
1 MET = 1 kcal per kg per hour (resting burn).
Example: 9.8 x 70 x 0.5 = 343 kcal.
howTo: Choose your activity from the list.
Pick metric (kg) or imperial (lb) and enter your body weight.
Enter how many minutes you did it.
Read the calories burned, the per-hour rate and the activity's MET value.
keyFacts: A MET (metabolic equivalent) measures activity intensity against resting burn.
1 MET equals about 1 kcal per kg per hour at rest.
The Compendium of Physical Activities catalogues MET values for hundreds of activities.
Running at 10 km/h is 9.8 MET; walking at 4 km/h is 3.5 MET.
Heavier people burn more calories for the same activity and duration.
A 70 kg person running 30 minutes at 10 km/h burns about 343 kcal.

calories-burned-calculator.workedExample:
70 kg, running at 10 km/h, 30 minutes:
1. MET value for running at 10 km/h = 9.8.
2. Hours = 30 / 60 = 0.5.
3. Calories = 9.8 x 70 x 0.5 = 343 kcal.
4. Per-hour rate = 9.8 x 70 = 686 kcal/hour.
